title: [Quality Management] Enforce rules and restrictions with indirect and implicit permissions
summary: Quality Management uses InherentPermissions so that, when no setup or triggered generation rule exists, users need no QM permissions. When a rule does trigger, users without QM permissions get a standard permission error instead of silently skipping inspection creation. A new 'QltyMgmt - I. Create' permission set grants the minimum indirect rights.
key_points: InherentPermissions used for the setup and generation rule tables so users without QM permissions are not blocked when nothing triggers
When a generation rule triggers, users without QM permissions now get a standard permission error instead of a silent skip
New permission set 'QltyMgmt - I. Create' grants indirect permissions to create inspections, including via Create Quality Inspection actions
Users with only that permission set cannot view or process inspections; View actions are hidden via AccessByPermission
quote: Implement InherentPermissions so users without QM permissions would not silently skip mandatory Quality Inspection creation or transaction restrictions.
